title: Detection of lung cancer using Kronecker mobile forward harmonic net
task: Lung cancer detection from CT images
comments: Hybrid approach combining MobileNet, Deep Kronecker Networks, and harmonic analysis shows strong performance but lacks external validation or comparison with state-of-the-art methods.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Integration of higher-order feature interactions via Deep Kronecker Networks improves lung cancer detection

title: Generalizable prediction of biological contaminants across aerobic and anaerobic membrane bioreactors
task: Prediction of bacterial and viral pathogen concentrations in membrane bioreactors
key_results: Improved generalization of predictions across aerobic and anaerobic MBRs at multiple sites; validated against WGAN baseline
comments: Lifelong learning with ensemble sequential data augmentation addresses nonstationarity well, but specific quantitative accuracy metrics are not provided.

outputs: bacterial cell and viral particle concentrations

hypotheses.result: EnSDA maintained robust performance across unseen treatment facilities and both aerobic/anaerobic systems

title: Alignment-free convolutional neural network classification of glycemic states in type 1 diabetes from GC–IMS breath spectra
task: Classification of glycemic states from breath spectra using CNN
key_results: 86.6% balanced accuracy (±4.0%), >92% specificity; robust to instrumental drift without alignment
comments: First CNN application to ion mobility spectrometry breath data with physiologically interpretable saliency maps, though small cohort (n=10) limits generalizability.

hypotheses.hypothesis: CNN can classify glycemic states from breath spectra without alignment preprocessing despite instrumental drift
hypotheses.result: Mean balanced accuracy 86.6% with stable performance across retention time variability

hypotheses.hypothesis: CNNs are more robust to spectral drift than traditional machine learning methods
hypotheses.result: CNN maintained performance without alignment while traditional models required extensive preprocessing

title: An improved Portia spider optimized SpikeApneaNet for ECG-based sleep apnea detection with FPGA implementation
task: ECG-based sleep apnea detection using spiking neural networks with FPGA implementation
key_results: 95.83% accuracy (subject-independent 5-fold CV), 94.53% mean accuracy on cross-dataset testing; 16 ms latency, 0.07 J energy consumption on FPGA
comments: Well-engineered framework combining spike-based deep learning with hardware implementation, though temporal spike encoding novelty relative to standard CNNs is incremental.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Improved Portia spider optimization enhances hyperparameter tuning and generalization across subjects
hypotheses.result: 95.83% accuracy with strong cross-dataset generalization (94.53% on UCDDB)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Spike-based encoding with spiking neural networks reduces computational complexity for edge deployment
hypotheses.result: 16 ms latency, 62.50 FPS, 14.53 FPS/W efficiency on FPGA with lower resource utilization than PSO baseline

title: Deepfakebuster: a confidence-calibrated adaptive ensemble framework for robust Deepfake image detection
task: Deepfake image detection via confidence-calibrated adaptive ensemble
key_results: 97.8% accuracy on 192,000 authentic and manipulated images; significantly outperforms individual detectors and static fusion baselines
comments: Novel reliability-aware adaptive fusion is promising, but evaluation limited to image domain; robustness to new synthesis methods not thoroughly tested.

model_io.model: DeepFakeBuster: heterogeneous ensemble fusing 5 detector types (spatial, boundary, noise, semantic, frequency-domain) with confidence-calibrated adaptive fusion

hypotheses.hypothesis: Reliability-aware adaptive fusion outperforms static ensemble averaging
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 97.8% accuracy; significant improvement over individual detectors and static baselines

title: A novel gas detector optimisation method combining 2-of-N voting systems, kinetic theory of gases, and exceedance curves to minimise CFD requirements
task: Gas detector optimization with reduced CFD simulations using kinetic theory and voting logic
key_results: Mathematical model estimates flammable cloud volume with accuracy comparable to CFD while significantly reducing computational time and simulations required
comments: Practical industrial application but lacks quantitative metrics (e.g., number of simulations saved, runtime reduction factors) in the abstract.

model_io.model: Kinetic theory-based mathematical model with Monte Carlo simulations and set covering optimization with 2-of-N voting constraints

hypotheses.hypothesis: Kinetic theory model with exceedance curves approximates CFD results while reducing computational burden
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: accuracy comparable to CFD with fewer simulations; 2-of-N voting improves system reliability

title: 2D-unsteady chaotic flows for mixing two different non-Newtonian fluids: optimization and flow control
task: Mixing of shear-thinning fluids in 2D unsteady chaotic mixer with protocol optimization
key_results: Continuous modulation 29%-39% faster mixing than alternating modulation; alternating saves 9%-25% energy; final mixture rheology governed by more viscous fluid
comments: Rigorous numerical study balancing practical trade-offs but limited to 2D; 3D effects and scalability to industrial-scale mixers not addressed.

model_io.model: 2D two-rod chaotic mixer with CFD simulations comparing continuous vs. alternating modulation protocols
inputs: Two shear-thinning fluids with distinct power-law indices

hypotheses.hypothesis: Continuous modulation achieves faster mixing than alternating modulation in shear-thinning fluids
Alternating modulation is more energy efficient than continuous modulation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 9%-25% energy savings with ALT protocol

title: Balancing privacy and accuracy: federated learning for multi-class student performance prediction with adaptive noise differential privacy
task: Multi-class student performance prediction with federated learning and privacy
key_results: Accuracy improved from 0.9432 to 0.9516, F1 score from 0.9428 to 0.9522 using adaptive noise differential privacy; average information entropy 0.6472 on OULAD dataset
comments: Strong empirical results but lacks theoretical analysis of privacy-utility trade-offs or convergence guarantees for the federated setting.

model_io.model: 9-layer CNN with federated learning and adaptive noise differential privacy
inputs: Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD) student records
outputs: Accuracy, precision, F1 score, information entropy metrics

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adaptive noise DP improves prediction accuracy compared to traditional DP
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: accuracy 0.9516 vs 0.9432, though entropy comparable (0.6472 vs 0.6406)

title: Visibility-driven compensation model for driver pupillary response in road tunnels: a GWO-XGBoost and SHAP-based interpretable framework
task: Predicting driver pupil diameter in tunnels via explainable machine learning with feature importance analysis
key_results: GWO-XGBoost achieves R²=0.914, MAPE=7.15% on test set; visibility identified as dominant factor, followed by color temperature, road illuminance, geometric parameters
comments: Well-designed field study with interpretability via SHAP, though causality claims require careful interpretation; visibility-driven compensation model provides theoretical grounding.

model_io.model: GWO-XGBoost optimized via grey wolf optimizer; interpretability via SHAP analysis; visibility-driven compensation model
inputs: Tunnel visibility, illuminance (road/sidewall), color temperature, distance, curvature radius, external time, eye-tracking pupil diameter

hypotheses.hypothesis: GWO-based hyperparameter optimization outperforms grid and random search
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: R²=0.914, MAPE=7.15% on test set; better than baseline models

hypotheses.hypothesis: Visibility is the primary driver of pupil response in tunnels
hypotheses.result: Confirmed by SHAP analysis; visibility dominant, followed by color temperature and illuminance

title: Robust field-free superconducting diode effect in FeTe0.55Se0.45
task: Observe field-free superconducting diode effect in iron-based superconductor
key_results: Robust nonreciprocal supercurrent in FeTe0.55Se0.45 at zero magnetic field
Second harmonic response amplitude comparable to first harmonic near Tc
comments: Strain/polarization-induced symmetry breaking mechanism avoids need for heterostructures, enabling practical device applications.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Finite-momentum pairing or magnetochiral anisotropy origin
hypotheses.result: Ruled out; even-in-field symmetry incompatible with these mechanisms

hypotheses.hypothesis: Local strain/polarization-induced symmetry breaking generates SDE
hypotheses.result: Confirmed as primary mechanism after excluding device geometry, thermal effects, chiral domains, extrinsic magnetic order
